lead: San Francisco plumbing deals with very old buildings, steep hills, soft water and earthquake rules. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across San Francisco.
risk: old cast-iron and galvanized pipes, sewer lateral breaks and water heater strapping
risk_short: old pipes, sewer laterals and water heaters
why: A large share of San Francisco's housing was built before 1940. Victorian and Edwardian homes often have galvanized supply lines, cast-iron stacks and old clay sewer laterals. Multi-unit buildings share stacks and risers.
Earthquake rules require strapped water heaters and flexible gas connectors. Steep lots and tight lots make sewer and water line work slow.
water: Most of San Francisco's water comes from the Hetch Hetchy Reservoir in Yosemite. It is very soft, so scale is rare, but soft water can be harder on old pipes.
tips: Strap your water heater for earthquakes.
Know where your gas shutoff is and keep a wrench by it.
Scope the sewer lateral before buying.
Check building rules before plumbing work in flats.
areas: PipeMend works in the Mission, the Sunset, the Richmond, Noe Valley, Haight-Ashbury, Bernal Heights, Pacific Heights and every other San Francisco neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the San Francisco Department of Building Inspection (DBI), and plumbing contractors need a CSLB license with a C-36 classification.

faq.q: Why do San Francisco water heaters need straps?
faq.a: California law requires water heaters to be braced or strapped to resist earthquakes. A tipped heater can break water and gas lines. Your plumber adds straps when a heater is installed.
